title: Watford sack Ed Still, 22nd head coach since 2014, after 83 days in charge
content:
Watford have sacked head coach Ed Still after winning just three of his 15 matches in charge.

Still, whose younger brother Will Still was sacked by Watford’s Championship rivals Southampton in November, was at Vicarage Road for less than three months and was their third head coach of the campaign.

The 35-year-old was Watford’s 22nd permanent head coach appointment, not including interims, since 2014. The club have developed a reputation for sacking and replacing coaches under the Pozzo family, who own the club.

Born in Belgium to English parents, Still had previously managed Charleroi, Eupen, Kortrijk and Anderlecht in the Belgian Pro League, with his move to Watford his first appointment in English football.

Still was appointed on a two-and-half-year contract on February 9 following the resignation of predecessor Javi Gracia, who had only arrived at the club that October to replace Paulo Pezzolano.

Watford slipped five places in the Championship standings to finish the season in 16th. Saturday’s four-goal defeat at home to Coventry City was Still’s final game in charge and marked their sixth defeat in seven matches.

The side finished the campaign 16 points from the top six and a promotion play-off place, and 10 clear of the relegation zone.

Watford will now begin a search for their 15th head coach appointment, not counting interim bosses, since September 2019 when Gracia left for the first time, and their 12th since the end of the 2020-21 season. The club will prepare for their fifth successive season in the Championship, having been relegated from the Premier League in 2022.
